text:
Liz: Morning — I want to propose a concrete proto for per-route KPI panels in Console. Core metrics: p50/p95/p99 token latency (token-level waterfall), throughput (requests/sec & tokens/sec), error rate, and KV-cache hit/miss. Also we need kernel-selection counts so we can correlate slow tails with suboptimal kernels.

Marc: +1. Do you have thoughts on sampling? full-token telemetry will be huge.

Liz: Agreed. Proposal: default token telemetry sampled at 1% for production routes; 100% for error traces and for any request flagged with tail latency > p95. KV/cache and error counters are emitted 100%. Kernel selection events are low-cardinality and emitted 100%.

Katie: Concern: Prometheus/TSDB cost. Suggest keeping histogram + aggregated counters instead of raw spans. We can emit latency histograms (ex: power-of-two buckets up to 16k tokens) and then compute quantiles via histogram_quantile. Also keep a 1m and 5m rolling rate.

Rick: For kernel selection we should tag metrics with (model, kernel_variant, seq_len_bucket). seq_len buckets: <64, 64-256, 256-1024, >1024. That will make it easy to show a heatmap. I can add select_kernel labels in the runtime where we pick kernels.

Sophie: For perf regression detection: alert when route p99 rises >20% vs 7d baseline for 15m AND absolute p99 > threshold. Playbook should include automatic canary rollback for Dedicated if latencies cross SLA.

Liz: Example PromQL snippets for the panel: 

```
sum(rate(redwood_route_tokens_latency_bucket[5m])) by (route, le)
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_route_tokens_latency_bucket[5m])) by (route, le))
(sum(rate(redwood_route_requests_total{status!~\"5..\"}[1m])) by (route))
(sum(rate(redwood_route_errors_total[1m])) by (route)) / (sum(rate(redwood_route_requests_total[1m])) by (route))
```

Marc: We also need KV cache metrics: `redwood_kv_cache_hits_total{route}`, `redwood_kv_cache_misses_total{route}`, and `redwood_kv_cache_lookup_duration_seconds_bucket`. Those let us compute effective hit-rate and avg lookup latency per route.

Katie: Could we add a per-route sampling toggle in Console so SEs can bump telemetry for a route (e.g., 100% for a customer investigation)? UI would need guardrails for cost and a cooldown.

Liz: Yes — add a small control in the Route settings: telemetry sampling slider + temporary override with audit log. We'll need a backend API and RBAC.

Rick: I will put up a runtime PR to: 1) emit kernel selection labels, 2) add seq_len_bucket tag, 3) hook telemetry sampling config into request path. ETA EOW.

Sophie: I'll draft alert rules and a runbook for p99 regressions. I'll include steps for investigating kernel/caching regressions and a checklist for rolling back model/kernel variants.

Marc: I'll do a quick cost analysis for 1% token sampling vs 0.1% and how histograms affect TSDB cardinality. Also look at retention tradeoffs.

DeployBot: deploy: telemetry-agent/v2 started to infra-canary (cv: 4ef6a2) :rocket:

Katie: I can mock up a Console panel layout — two rows: left: per-route summary (p50/p95/p99, req/s, tokens/s, err%), right: waterfall drilldown (token-level stacked breakdown + kernel heatmap). Link to Figma in #design once ready.

Liz: Great. Assignments: Rick (runtime labels + sampling hook), Marc (TSDB cost calc + retention plan), Katie (Console panel + sampling UI), Sophie (alerts + runbook). I'll follow up with a short RFC doc that includes the PromQLs and panel mockups. Thanks :thumbsup:

Marc: +1, thanks everyone.

Sophie: leaving notes in the alerts doc now.

Rick: starting the runtime branch.
